scenes.line1: Why do modules matter in JS?
scenes.say: What’s the difference between JavaScript module systems, and why should you care?

scenes.label: ESM
scenes.sub: Uses import and export, works in browsers and Node twelve and up.
scenes.say: ECMAScript modules use import and export. They’re native in browsers and modern Node.

scenes.label: CommonJS
scenes.sub: Uses require and module.exports, standard in older Node.js.
scenes.say: CommonJS uses require and module exports. It’s the standard for older Node projects.
ESM uses import and export, while CommonJS relies on require and module exports.
ESM is great for new projects. It’s supported in browsers, allows static analysis, and works well with modern tools.

scenes.question: Can you mix ESM and CommonJS easily?
scenes.right: Mixing them can cause issues. You need extra setup or tools to bridge the gap.
scenes.say: Don’t assume you can mix ESM and CommonJS without trouble. They need special setup to work together.
